content:
Hello IQSS team. Good afternoon!

I've been looking at the recent issues that have been popping up on the GitHub issues page. Very specifically one, regarding default custom licenses preventing dataset creation. This is a good example of a bug/case that can be turning into a test preventing this from ever happening again. I discussed this very briefly with Phil. I want to help in whatever way I can to prevent the team from firefighting bugs.

I strongly believe that having a pipeline for bug -> fix -> test will help make Dataverse resilient over time and make it anti-fragile. I wasn't entirely sure on where to go from having the idea, and was hoping that the IQSS team could provide some recommendations on whether this is a good idea and if it is, where can we go from here? Maybe a board/doc that lists these bugs that are suitable for being turned into tests? In an ideal world, I would want to establish a repeatable process for resolving these issues, writing some replication bullets, and put them in a backlog for test implementations.

@Ash Manda sounds like a great topic for tech hours! Would you like to lead a discussion on this some day?

Also, did you mean to have JSF in the Zulip topic? The approach sound reusable across a variety of contexts.
I would love to! I initially only envisioned this being used for the JSF tests, but if y'all can find more use for the process, then I'm more than glad to pitch in. That's why I had JSF in the topic.
Cool. I added it to the agenda for next week but it can be whenever.
